title: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
caption: Terracotta dreams
subtitle: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by the ancient Greeks and long associated with the Italian House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, its layered past remains visible throughout this coastal city in the south of France, where historic architecture meets the blue waters of the Mediterranean and the sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

title: The chapel and hermitage of Santa Justa in Cantabria, Spain
caption: Shelter among the waves
subtitle: The chapel and hermitage of Santa Justa in Cantabria, Spain
description: Tucked into the rugged coastline of northern Spain, the 16th-century Hermitage of Santa Justa, featured in today's image, overlooks the crashing waves of the Cantabrian Sea. Built partly into the rock and associated with the relics of Saints Justa and Rufina, the small chapel eventually became a pilgrimage site. Its sheltered stone walls create a striking contrast with the powerful waves and rugged cliffs around it.

title: Fiddlehead fern
caption: Geometry in nature
subtitle: Fibonacci Day
description: Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In maths, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Today is Fibonacci Day, chosen for the numbers of the date (11/23) to honour the sequence. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.

title: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Highlands, Scotland
caption: Autumnal camouflage
subtitle: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Scotland
description: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and more recently planted conifer woodlands, providing valuable habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts and other tasty morsels throughout the year. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.

title: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA
caption: When snow meets red rock
subtitle: Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah
description: Snow transforms Bryce Canyon National Park, blanketing the landscape in white while its fiery orange-red hoodoos rise above the snowy terrain. Seen from Sunset Point, one of the park's best-known viewpoints, these fantastical shapes are part of the Claron Formation, a collection of sedimentary rocks deposited around 50 million years ago and later sculpted by weathering and erosion. Because much of the park lies above 2,440 metres, snow can arrive as early as October. In today's image, snow clings to the canyon's ridges and spires while mist drifts across the cliffs, creating an iconic winter scene in the American Southwest.

title: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hilo, Hawaii, USA
caption: Where rainbows fall
subtitle: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hawaii
description: Water, sunlight and lush greenery come together at Rainbow Falls in Hilo, on the island of Hawaii. Here, the Wailuku River plunges around 24 metres over a lava ledge, sending mist into the air as it reaches the pool below. On sunny mornings, the mist can catch the light and produce the colourful rainbows that gave the falls their name. Known in Hawaiian as Waiānuenue, meaning 'rainbow water', this striking waterfall is surrounded by tropical vegetation and has a special place in Hawaiian legend.

title: Butte at sunset, Face Canyon, Lake Powell, Utah, USA
caption: Ribbons of grey and gold
subtitle: Face Canyon, Lake Powell, Utah
description:
Hidden within an ancient sandstone landscape, Face Canyon is one of 96 canyons stretching out from Lake Powell in southern Utah. Many are far from roads and would be difficult to reach if they hadn't been flooded by the lake, which was created in 1963 during the construction of the Glen Canyon Dam. The lake's waters extend for around 186 miles (299 kilometres), along creeks and canyons which you can explore by boat, kayak or jet ski.
Lake Powell took 17 years to fill to its highest water level and is the second-largest human-made lake in the United States. It is also a contender for the most scenic, boasting blue waters surrounded by sandstone walls. You may need to paddle your way to these serene sunset views, but the journey is part of the adventure. And if you arrive when the sun is at its peak, Face Canyon's high cliff walls will provide some welcome relief from the desert sun.

title: Old town and Vltava River, Prague, Czechia
caption: Bridges through time
description: This autumn view from Letná Park looks out over Prague, which was built along the banks of the Vltava River in Czechia. In today's image, the river winds its way through the historic Old Town and Malá Strana districts, beneath Mánes Bridge in the foreground. Many beautiful bridges now span the Vltava, but for centuries there was only one: Charles Bridge, pictured second from the bottom. Its first stones were laid in 1357 during the reign of Charles IV and, until 1841, it was the only way to cross the river on foot. Today, its stone arches, Gothic towers and statues lining the bridge draw large crowds, so visitors are advised to arrive by dawn for the best photographs. Alternatively, they could walk on to the next crossing, Legion Bridge, which is less crowded and offers beautiful views of the National Theatre, Prague Castle and its busier neighbour.
